title: Another U.S. appellate court goes against Kalshi, building the industry's legal headwinds
summary: Despite a Commodity Futures Trading Commission demand that prediction markets return to operating in all 50 states, federal courts continue to get in the way.
content: A U.S. appellate court has ruled against Kalshi, adding to growing legal challenges for the prediction market industry. Despite a Commodity Futures Trading Commission demand for prediction markets to operate across all 50 states, federal courts continue to create roadblocks for the platform's expansion and operations.
content_ta: Kalshi நிறுவனத்திற்கு எதிராக ஒரு U.S. appellate நீதிமன்றம் தீர்ப்பளித்துள்ளது, இது prediction market துறைக்கு மேலும் சட்ட சிக்கல்களை உருவாக்குகிறது. அனைத்து 50 மாநிலங்களிலும் prediction markets தொடர்ந்து செயல்பட வேண்டும் என்ற Commodity Futures Trading Commission இன் கோரிக்கை இருந்தபோதிலும், இந்த தளத்தின் விரிவாக்கத்திற்கு கூட்டாட்சி நீதிமன்றங்கள் தொடர்ந்து தடைைகளை உருவாக்குகின்றன.

title: Trump administration unveils new center to choke off scam payments
summary: Americans reported more than $17.7 billion in online fraud losses in 2025.
content: The Trump administration has unveiled a new center aimed at choking off scam payments. The initiative comes as online fraud continues to pose a major challenge for consumers, following reports of massive financial losses by Americans totaling more than $17.7 billion.
content_ta: Trump administration மோசடி கட்டணங்களைத் தடுப்பதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்ட புதிய மையம் ஒன்றை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. Americans $17.7 பில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமான ஆன்லைன் மோசடி இழப்புகளைப் புகாரளித்துள்ள நிலையில், இந்த புதிய நடவடிக்கை எடுக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Fed officials saw October rate hold as a ‘close call,’ minutes show
summary: The latest FOMC minutes suggest greater appetite for higher rates than the Fed’s 10–2 vote indicated, with markets now pricing in a December hike.
content: Recently released Fed minutes revealed that the October interest rate hold was considered a close call by officials. The Federal Open Market Committee discussion indicated a stronger appetite for higher borrowing costs than the initial 10-2 vote suggested. Following the publication of these minutes, financial markets have begun increasingly pricing in the possibility of a rate hike in December.
content_ta: வெளியிடப்பட்ட Fed கூட்டத்தின் குறிப்புகளின்படி, அக்டோபர் வட்டி விகிதத்தை மாற்றாமல் வைத்திருப்பது மிகவும் நெருக்கமான முடிவு என்று அதிகாரிகள் கருதினர். ஆரம்பத்தில் பதிவான 10-2 வாக்கு எண்ணிக்கையை விட, அதிக வட்டி விகிதங்களுக்கு ஆதரவு அதிகம் இருந்ததை இந்த விவாதங்கள் காட்டுகின்றன. இந்த அறிக்கையைத் தொடர்ந்து, டிசம்பர் மாதத்தில் வட்டி உயர்த்தப்படலாம் என்று நிதிச் சந்தைகள் கணிக்கத் தொடங்கியுள்ளன.

title: Standard Chartered, StraitsX, OCBC complete trial of tokenized deposit interoperability
summary: The companies said that unlocking the full potential of 'always-on' tokenized deposits requires interoperability across platforms.
content: Standard Chartered, StraitsX, and OCBC have successfully completed a trial focusing on the interoperability of tokenized deposits. The participating companies noted that unlocking the full potential of these always-on digital financial instruments requires seamless interoperability across different platforms and systems.
content_ta: Standard Chartered, StraitsX மற்றும் OCBC ஆகியவை டோக்கன் செய்யப்பட்ட டெபாசிட்டுகளின் இயங்குதன்மை தொடர்பான சோதனையை வெற்றிகரமாக நிறைவு செய்துள்ளன. எப்போதும் செயல்பாட்டில் இருக்கும் இந்த டிஜிட்டல் நிதி கருவிகளின் முழு திறனையும் வெளிக்கொணர பல்வேறு தளங்கள் முழுவதும் தடையற்ற இயங்குதன்மை தேவை என்று சம்பந்தப்பட்ட நிறுவனங்கள் குறிப்பிட்டுள்ளன.

title: Bitcoin launches Testnet5 and gives miners a real trial of four proposed fixes
summary:
Mining pools can test the blocks their software builds while Bitcoin Core and Sparrow Wallet prepare support.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Bitcoin has launched Testnet5, providing miners with a real trial of four proposed protocol fixes. This release allows mining pools to test the blocks generated by their software. Meanwhile, Bitcoin Core and Sparrow Wallet are preparing to offer full support for the new testnet environment, helping improve overall network stability and testing procedures.
content_ta: Bitcoin தனது Testnet5-ai அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது, இது மைனர்களுக்கு நான்கு முன்மொழியப்பட்ட திருத்தங்களைச் சோதிக்க உண்மையான வாய்ப்பை வழங்குகிறது. மைனிங் பூக்கள் தங்கள் மென்பொருளால் உருவாக்கப்பட்ட பிளாக்குகளை இதன் மூலம் சோதிக்கலாம். இதற்கிடையில், Bitcoin Core மற்றும் Sparrow Wallet ஆகியவை புதிய டெஸ்ட்நெட் சூழலுக்கான ஆதரவைத் தயாரிக்கத் தொடங்கியுள்ளன.

title: Binance Plans Expansion into 5 Asian Markets
summary: Binance plans to reveal details of its upcoming Asian expansion in early 2027.
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has announced plans to expand its operations into five Asian markets. Company representatives stated that specific details regarding this upcoming regional growth strategy will be officially revealed in early 2027. This move represents a significant step for the platform as it seeks to strengthen its presence and increase its user base across the Asian region.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி பரிமாற்ற நிறுவனமான Binance, ஐந்து ஆசிய சந்தைகளில் தனது சேவைகளை விரிவுபடுத்த திட்டமிட்டுள்ளதாக அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த வரவிருக்கும் ஆசிய விரிவாக்கம் குறித்த கூடுதல் விவரங்கள் 2027 ஆம் ஆண்டின் தொடக்கத்தில் வெளியிடப்படும் என்று நிறுவனத்தின் பிரதிநிதிகள் தெரிவித்துள்ளனர். ஆசிய பிராந்தியத்தில் தனது இருப்பை வலுப்படுத்தவும், பயனர்களின் எண்ணிக்கையை அதிகரிக்கவும் இந்த நடவடிக்கை உதவும்.

title: What is Ethereum actually for? A judge and Vitalik Buterin both left it open
summary: As a judge acquits the Peraire-Bueno brothers, Bitwise's Hunter Horsley and Vitalik Buterin weigh in on what crypto is actually for.
content: Following the acquittal of the Peraire-Bueno brothers by a judge, industry figures including Bitwise's Hunter Horsley and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin have shared their perspectives on the practical purpose and utility of cryptocurrency, leaving the broader question open-ended.
content_ta: Peraire-Bueno சகோதரர்கள் நீதிமன்றத்தால் விடுதலை செய்யப்பட்டதை தொடர்ந்து, Bitwise நிறுவனத்தின் Hunter Horsley மற்றும் Ethereum இணை நிறுவனர் Vitalik Buterin உள்ளிட்ட துறை சார்ந்த தலைவர்கள் கிரிப்டோகரன்சியின் உண்மையான நோக்கம் மற்றும் பயன்பாடு குறித்து தங்கள் கருத்துக்களை பகிர்ந்துள்ளனர்.

title: Is MicroStrategy’s 12% Dividend Safe? Its $100 Stock Just Broke Again
summary:
MicroStrategy's 12% dividend stock STRC broke below $100 as Bitcoin dipped under $63,000. Here is where the payout stands.
The post Is MicroStrategy’s 12% Dividend Safe? Its $100 Stock Just Broke Again appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: MicroStrategy's 12% dividend stock, STRC, dropped below $100 as Bitcoin fell under $63,000. Investors are closely watching the safety of the high payout amid the broader cryptocurrency market decline affecting the company's valuation and share price.
content_ta: Bitcoin விலை 63,000 டாலருக்கு கீழே சரிந்ததை அடுத்து, MicroStrategy நிறுவனத்தின் 12 சதவீத டிவிடெண்ட் பங்கு STRC 100 டாலருக்கு கீழே சரிந்துள்ளது. இந்த சரிவு முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மத்தியில் அதன் பேஅவுட் பாதுகாப்பு குறித்த கேள்விகளை எழுப்பியுள்ளது.

title: Nvidia Moves Up Raises and Stock Grants After Jensen Huang Exit
summary:
Nvidia moves staff raises and stock grants to December after Jensen Huang's exit as employees press the board on its CEO search.
The post Nvidia Moves Up Raises and Stock Grants After Jensen Huang Exit appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Nvidia has advanced its schedule for staff raises and stock grants to December following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang. The decision comes as employees actively press the company's board regarding the ongoing search for a new chief executive officer to lead the tech giant moving forward.
content_ta: CEO Jensen Huang-ன் வெளியேற்றத்தைத் தொடர்ந்து, Nvidia நிறுவனம் தனது ஊழியர்களுக்கான சம்பள உயர்வு மற்றும் பங்கு வழங்கல் கால அட்டவணையை டிசம்பர் மாதத்திற்கு முன்னோக்கி நகர்த்தியுள்ளது. புதிய தலைமைச் நிர்வாக அதிகாரியைத் தேர்ந்தெடுக்கும் பணி குறித்து ஊழியர்கள் வாரியத்தை வலியுறுத்தி வரும் சூழலில் இந்த முடிவு எடுக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: What Is Bitcoin's Power Law and Why Are Analysts Concerned About $62K Support?
summary:
Bitcoin's Power Law support line sits near $62K, says Fidelity's Jurrien Timmer. See why analysts are watching closely.

content: Fidelity's Jurrien Timmer has highlighted Bitcoin's Power Law support line, which currently sits near the $62,000 price level. Analysts are closely monitoring this key technical threshold to understand the cryptocurrency's potential future price trajectory and market stability.
content_ta: Fidelity-ஐச் சேர்ந்த Jurrien Timmer, Bitcoin-ன் Power Law ஆதரவு கோடு சுமார் $62,000 விலைப் பகுதியில் உள்ளதாகத் தெரிவித்துள்ளார். கிரிப்டோகரன்சியின் எதிர்கால விலை போக்கு மற்றும் சந்தை நிலைத்தன்மையைப் புரிந்துகொள்ள ஆய்வாளர்கள் இந்த முக்கியமான தொழில்நுட்ப எல்லையை உன்னிப்பாகக் கவனித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: Nvidia’s $500B chip-financing plan stalled, no deals before 2027: WSJ
summary:
Nvidia's stalled financing plan may dampen investor confidence, potentially affecting its stock performance and market valuation outlook.
The post Nvidia’s $500B chip-financing plan stalled, no deals before 2027: WSJ appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Nvidia’s reported $500 billion chip-financing plan has reportedly stalled, with no deals expected before 2027, according to the Wall Street Journal. This delay in the massive financing initiative could dampen investor confidence in the technology sector, potentially impacting Nvidia's stock performance and overall market valuation outlook as market participants reassess their growth expectations for the dominant chipmaker.
content_ta: Wall Street Journal வெளியிட்ட தகவலின்படி, Nvidia நிறுவனத்தின் $500 பில்லியன் சிப்-நிதித் திட்டம் தற்காலிகமாக நிறுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளதாகவும், 2027-க்கு முன்பு எந்த ஒப்பந்தங்களும் இருக்காது என்றும் கூறப்படுகிறது. இந்த பெரிய நிதித் திட்டத்தின் தாமதம் முதலீட்டாளர்களின் நம்பிக்கையைக் குறைக்கக்கூடும், மேலும் இது Nvidia நிறுவனத்தின் பங்குச் சந்தை செயல்திறனையும் சந்தை மதிப்பீட்டையும் பாதிக்கலாம்.

title: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol arrive with noticeably different personalities
summary:
The shift towards shorter, more confident responses in GPT-6.2 models may reduce user guidance, impacting decision-making and reliability.
The post OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol arrive with noticeably different personalities appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: OpenAI has launched its new GPT-6.2 models, named Astra and Sol, featuring noticeably different personalities. The update introduces shorter and more confident responses, which may reduce user guidance and impact decision-making and reliability. The release marks a continued evolution in how AI models interact with their users across various applications.
content_ta: OpenAI தனது புதிய GPT-6.2 மாடல்களான Astra மற்றும் Sol ஆகியவற்றை வெளியிட்டுள்ளது. இவை குறிப்பிடத்தக்க அளவில் மாறுபட்ட ஆளுமைகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளன. இந்த அப்டேட் மூலம் குறுகிய மற்றும் மிகவும் உறுதியான பதில்கள் வழங்கப்படுகின்றன. இது பயனர்களின் வழிகாட்டுதலைக் குறைத்து, முடிவெடுக்கும் திறன் மற்றும் நம்பகத்தன்மையை பாதிக்கக்கூடும்.

title: Trump administration taps TRM Labs in $95 million push to disrupt crypto crime networks
summary:
The initiative could significantly enhance federal capabilities in combating international crypto crime, potentially recovering billions in losses.

content: The Trump administration has partnered with TRM Labs through a multi-million dollar initiative aimed at disrupting international cryptocurrency crime networks. content_ta: சர்வதேச கிரிப்டோ குற்ற வலைப்பின்னல்களை முறியடிக்கும் நோக்கில் பல மில்லியன் டாலர் மதிப்பிலான திட்டத்தின் கீழ் TRM Labs நிறுவனத்துடன் Trump நிர்வாகம் கூட்டு சேர்ந்துள்ளது. இந்த முயற்சியானது டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து தொடர்பான குற்றங்களை எதிர்த்துப் போராடுவதிலும், சட்டவிரோதமான இழப்புகளை மீட்டெடுப்பதிலும் மத்திய அமைப்புகளின் திறன்களை கணிசமாக மேம்படுத்தும் என்று எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது.

title: BOJ’s Ueda warns rising oil prices, weak yen may hit Japan’s economy
summary:
Japan's economic stability faces challenges as inflationary pressures and currency depreciation may necessitate shifts in monetary policy.
The post BOJ’s Ueda warns rising oil prices, weak yen may hit Japan’s economy appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda has warned that rising oil prices and a weak yen could negatively impact the Japanese economy. These inflationary pressures and currency challenges may influence future monetary policy decisions as the central bank monitors economic stability closely.
content_ta: Japan's economy பாதிக்கப்படலாம் என்று BOJ தலைவர் Ueda எச்சரித்துள்ளார். உயர்ந்துவரும் எண்ணெய் விலைகள் மற்றும் பலவீனமான yen மதிப்பு ஆகியவை நாட்டின் பொருளாதார ஸ்திரத்தன்மைக்கு சவாலாக இருக்கலாம் என்றும், இது எதிர்கால நாணய கொள்கை முடிவுகளை பாதிக்கலாம் என்றும் அவர் தெரிவித்துள்ளார்.

title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Accounting with plugins for QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite and more
summary:
OpenAI's move into accounting automation could streamline financial operations, but human oversight remains crucial for accuracy.
The post OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Accounting with plugins for QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite and more appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Accounting, featuring plugins for major platforms like QuickBooks, Xero, and NetSuite. This new tool aims to streamline financial operations and automation. Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. It adds to OmenX’s intraday offering, which spans prediction horizons from 30 seconds to 24 hours, depending on the market. Beyond crypto, OmenX offers directional prediction markets linked to more than 100 global assets, including U.S. equities, futures, ETFs and indices. Its event markets also cover live sports and esports, with sports coverage spanning major football leagues, basketball, American football, ice hockey, baseball and UFC. Leverage has been central to OmenX’s platform from the outset, allowing traders to amplify their exposure on supported event markets. The latest launch builds on that foundation while advancing a broader goal: making prediction markets a practical financial tool for retail users. OmenX organizes the trading decision around a defined question: will an asset’s price be higher or lower at the end of a specified period? Users can express a directional view without purchasing the underlying asset, targeting an exact closing price or constructing an options position that requires decisions about strikes, implied volatility and time decay. “Leverage has been part of OmenX from the start, but our ambition goes beyond adding leverage to prediction markets,” said James, founder and CEO of OmenX. “We want to make global markets easier to participate in. OmenX plans to expand its coverage of traditional and crypto assets while deepening the trading experience across supported markets. title: Nomupay Joins AWS ISV Accelerate Program

The program helps AWS Partners drive new business by directly connecting participating ISVs with the AWS Sales organization.   
The Nomupay platform brings acceptance, payouts, and reporting together via a single platform, providing enterprises with a single integration and contract, rather than a patchwork of providers. The problem that enterprises scaling in APAC and EMEA often face is that every new market brings its own acquirer, integrations, local payment methods, and compliance consideration; and, often, a separate route for paying out partners and suppliers. Merchants can also pay out cross-border in 40+ markets across Europe and Asia, with flexible fund flows and treasury management. Nomupay holds local acquiring licences across Europe and APAC, giving merchants direct market access, reducing reliance on third-party networks. 
Nomupay uses Amazon Bedrock across its payout operations and merchant onboarding, applying generative AI to payment investigations and compliance review with sensitive data redacted, full audit trails and human approval built in. Nomupay is a PCI DSS Level 1 certified service provider, and uses AWS services including Lambda, EMR, API Gateway, AWS ECS, DynamoDB , Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow, AWS RDS, AWS Kinesis and Bedrock. 
Mark Stannard, Chief Business Officer, Nomupay, says, “Every enterprise we speak to wants to grow into new markets without taking on a new payment provider for each one. Nomupay utilises Amazon Bedrock to add generative AI to payment investigations and compliance review, with a human in the loop. We are excited to bring these advanced solutions to merchants via AWS Marketplace"
The AWS ISV Accelerate Program provides Nomupay with co-sell support and benefits to meet customer needs through collaboration with AWS field sellers globally. Co-selling provides better customer outcomes and assures mutual commitment from AWS and its partners.  
AWS ISV Accelerate Program members are held to the industry’s highest standards and must undergo a comprehensive evaluation to gain acceptance into the program. title: Mastercard and Ant International Advance Trusted Agentic Commerce in Asia Pacific
summary:
Mastercard today announced two milestones that advance trusted agentic commerce in Asia Pacific: a live consumer transaction through Antom, Ant International's merchant payment and digitalization platform, demonstrating how AI agents can act on verified consumer instructions; and a completed Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines (AP4M) pilot with Antom in Singapore, demonstrating how businesses can control and authorize purchases made by their AI agents.
As agentic commerce moves from experimentation toward real-world adoption, AI agents are increasingly positioned to act and transact on behalf of consumers and businesses. Together, Mastercard and Ant International are helping address a critical requirement for this emerging ecosystem: the ability to verify an agent's identity and authority to act. Whether an agent is shopping for a consumer or purchasing services for a business, there needs to be a reliable way to establish who it represents, what it has permission to do and whether it is acting within those parameters.
Proving what a consumer authorized
In the live transaction, an AI agent purchased a cup of coffee based on the consumer's pre-captured intent, with acceptance supported by Antom. The transaction ran on Mastercard Agent Pay with Verifiable Intent, creating a verifiable record of what the consumer had authorized the agent to do.
Mastercard Agent Pay brings together capabilities including network tokenization, authentication and consumer intent to enable secure and trusted agentic payments. As part of this framework, Verifiable Intent is designed as an open, standards-based and protocol-agnostic trust layer that helps merchants and other participants establish trust in agent-initiated transactions by making consumer authorization verifiable.
Extending the same principle to business payments
For businesses, the same challenge takes a different form: how to delegate purchasing authority to an AI agent while maintaining control over what it can buy and how much it can spend. As agents increasingly transact directly with digital services and other machines, payments also need to keep pace with the speed of machine commerce.
 
Introduced in June this year, Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines enables businesses to credential their AI agents, define what those agents are authorized to purchase and spend and enforce those limits at the point of payment. Every transaction leaves an auditable record, and merchants can identify which business an agent represents.
Building on Mastercard's recent live demonstration of AP4M at Cloudflare Connect, the completed pilot in Singapore tested the identity, governance and payment controls businesses need to delegate routine purchasing to agents with confidence. Antom enabled the AI agent to successfully use AP4M's credentialing, policy controls and payment authorization capabilities to purchase digital services within parameters set by the business.
“AI agents are already capable of completing payments. The bigger challenge now is creating the trust for consumers, businesses and merchants to embrace them,” said Joyce Bo, Executive Vice President, Core Payments, Asia Pacific, Mastercard. “Together with Ant International, we’re putting the safeguards needed for agentic commerce into practice across consumer and business payments. By giving people and businesses greater control over what their agents are authorized to do, we can help move agentic commerce from concept to adoption at scale.”
Building trust as agentic commerce scales
Together, the two milestones demonstrate how the same fundamental principles of identity, authorization and accountability apply whether an AI agent is acting for a consumer or a business. Antom brings together consumer payment and merchant acceptance capabilities to help put these principles into practice.
“We’re pleased to work with Mastercard to help merchants succeed in agentic commerce. Our collaboration lets merchants confidently accept purchases from AI agents acting within consumer- or business-approved permissions. That trust creates a foundation for merchants to rethink how they deliver value — from reaching more customers through AI agents to offering services in smaller, flexible units that agents can discover, combine and purchase, opening up new business models. Powered by Ant International's full-stack, AI-native solutions across payments, accounts, FX, treasury and growth operations, we aim to help merchants turn AI capabilities into practical business value — serving customers better, managing operations more efficiently, and preparing for new opportunities as commerce evolves in the agentic era,” said Chunmao Zhu, VP, Technology & Business, Antom.  
Through their work together, Mastercard and Ant International are putting these capabilities into practice while helping advance an open, interoperable approach to agentic commerce as adoption grows.

title: Visa Unveils Next Generation of Subscription Management Solutions With Visa Recurrent
summary:

It enables consumers to view and manage recurring payments through their financial institution’s digital banking experiences, giving them greater visibility and control over recurring payments, at the same time helping financial institutions and merchants deliver more seamless payment experiences.
Visa also announced that Kiwibank is the first issuer globally to deploy Visa Recurrent through its mobile banking app and internet banking, to help give Kiwibank customers a simpler way to understand and manage recurring payments commitments on a channel they already use and trust.

It's an exciting milestone and a great example of what can be achieved when organisations work together with a clear focus on customer outcomes.”
Meet Visa Recurrent: More Control, Less Hassle
From streaming and fitness memberships to software and household bills, recurring payments have become a part of everyday life. Yet managing those commitments can still require navigating multiple websites, apps, and customer-service channels. Through participating financial institutions, Visa Recurrent enables consumers to access a consolidated view of eligible recurring payments and take supported actions directly within their digital banking experience.
For participating merchants, Visa Recurrent creates a more connected way to manage customer relationships throughout the recurring payment lifecycle. When consumers take supported actions through their financial institution, merchants may receive timely notifications and use redirects to engage the customer directly.
“Consumers shouldn’t have to hunt across websites, apps and customer service channels just to understand or manage their subscriptions,” said T.R. Ramachandran, Head of Products and Solutions, Asia Pacific, Visa. “Visa Recurrent helps financial institutions bring that visibility and control into the digital banking experiences consumers already use and trust. This makes recurring payments easier to manage while giving banks another way to strengthen their everyday relationship with customers.”
Built for the Way People Pay Today
Consumers increasingly expect simple ways to manage recurring payments, while merchants and financial institutions need clearer signals to manage those relationships efficiently. According to Visa research, one in three New Zealand consumers say they've continued paying for a service they no longer use, and 86% want their bank to provide tools that help them manage recurring payments. Visa Recurrent responds to that demand by enabling participating financial institutions to provide a more connected management experience through their existing digital channels.

title: Update Settlement Infrastructure for New Games, Build a Multi-Rail Trust Layer, and Close the Accessibility Gap in the AI Economy: Ant International’s Peng Yang at SFF 2026
summary:
Speaking at the 2026 Singapore FinTech Festival, Ant International’s CEO Peng Yang argued that our settlement infrastructure needs to evolve beyond today’s four-party payments model to assign effectively roles and responsibilities.
Ant International processed the equivalent of 1.1 trillion USD on its WhaleRTP blockchain settlement network in the last 12 months in collaboration with 23 leading global banks; expected to double in 2027.
He also said that agentic economy needs to rest on a stronger multi-rail, multi-modal and multi-asset trust layer, and that good AI solutions design can power a new, more inclusive globalization project by putting the little guys on a level playing field.

Ant International at the Singapore Fintech Festival 2026
At the Singapore FinTech Festival, Ant International CEO Peng Yang (YP) joined Swift’s Javier Pérez-Tasso and HSBC’s Surendra Rosha for the panel “From Digital to Intelligent: Who Will Build the Next Financial System?”, moderated by Arjun Vir Singh of Arthur D. Little.
YP highlighted three critical angles to tackle the future financial system: 
How should settlement infrastructure evolve in the AI + blockchain era to establish new game rules? 
How to build cross-rail, cross-modal trust for the agentic economy? 
How to mainstream inclusion into AI design to close the accessibility gap for SMEs? 

Peng Yang (R), CEO of Ant International, speaks at the Singapore Fintech Festival 2026.
The Missing Debate: Rewiring settlement infrastructure
The four-party payment model — issuer, acquirer, network, regulator — has served as a mature bedrock for traditional economy. However, would we still need the acquirer or the network as we know it when CBDCs, blockchain and web3 currencies go mainstream? 
Yang argued the industry should brace for new post-4-party models of accountability and new game rules for a world increasingly dominated by account-to-account transactions as merchants begin to run entire transactions on a rail built on tokenization. 
“The settlement layer, the invisible rail—still matters most. Only at this layer can new rules of the game be defined, so everyone plays on the expanded field with clear responsibilities and new boundaries.” 
While pushing the intelligence and application frontiers of AI and blockchain, Ant International felt strongly that its settlement infrastructure needed to evolve, so trust and responsibility can be effectively assigned inside new forms of regulated businesses. 
The shift is already visible. On WhaleRTP, Ant International’s blockchain platform connecting 23 leading global and regional banks, the company settled the equivalent of USD 1.1 trillion in last 12 months. The processing volume is likely to double in 2027.
But the ledger itself is not the challenge. 
“Blockchain is not rocket science,” he said. The hard parts are compliance, the business mechanism, and proving the authenticity of the assets on the rail. To achieve that, banks, fintechs and partners such as Swift need to work together.
The trust layer: no one builds it alone in the multi-rail, multi-modal age
Such foundational technology and institutional changes require a new trust layer. Yang cited a top priority for agentic commerce: KYA – or Know Your Agent. Financial institutions used to run separate, siloed KYC structures. In the KYA era, monitoring and verification happen around the clock across rails and networks. Ant International’s own KYA interoperability framework with Visa and Mastercard is a timely move in that direction. 

Ant International CEO Peng Yang speaks on a panel at Singapore Fintech Festival 2026
The encouraging part, Yang said, is how fast collaboration can move. Ant International proposed the bank-to-wallet direct remit idea to Swift; eight months later it was live, moving funds from a Standard Chartered account to a DANA wallet in seven seconds — a pace that is rare across a field of many private-sector partners.
“We don’t want to do everything ourselves,” Yang said. “Seven years ago nothing existed, so we had to — that’s how Whale was built. Today Swift is building, JP Morgan is building, Citi is building, some countries run fast payment systems, and networks are forming across Southeast Asia.”
In the future, Yang believes there will be an open, connected network where AI picks the best route for each merchant — fastest or cheapest. Builders of the intelligence layer like Ant International would need rails to be open and reliable so each player can use them on behalf of its own clients.
The accessibility gap: if only big tech captures the AI bonus, “that future is boring”
“If technology fast-forwards and only the big enterprises and big tech companies capture the AI premium, that future is boring,” Yang said. Technology has to be democratized so that SMEs and the little guys share in the benefit, not only the largest firms.
Globalization 1.0, while creating unprecedented wealth and prosperity by bringing productivity gains to large enterprises, has left many small businesses, individuals and communities behind, leading to today’s fragmentation. To move the world forward, our re-globalization project has to ensure broader inclusion of the smallest participants. 
From Ant International’s perspective, artificial intelligence – when proactively engineered – will make the task possible. “In our products and solutions design, Ai can narrow the distance between large and small: with agent help, a small enterprise or an individual can compete with the giants.”
From AI breakthroughs to Grassroots Empowerment
In an afternoon session, “Driving Financial Inclusion and Shared Prosperity in an Age of Uncertainty”, Yang recalled a trek through northern Iraq on the Abraham’s Path project, where he and his colleagues saw what connectivity and access to technology, information and choice meant for a remote mountain village. He closed with two ambitions.
“First, payment should be like the internet and email — nobody asks whether an email is domestic or international; the internet killed the concept of a border. Payments still draw a distinct line between local and cross-border. With agentic, with tokenization, with public-private initiatives for interoperability, we should remove those differences — so even the most remote people can enjoy borderless payment, remittance and purchase, online and offline.” YP told fellow panelists, William Ury, Professor at Harvard Law School, Alexandre Chade, Founder & Chairman of Dotz, and Luay Obaidi, and Chief Product Officer, Qi Card.
“Second, if a small player has a big dream, they should be able to access the financial support they need to thrive — with new wallets and financial institutions empowered by technology, that should become the new normal of our economy.”

title: Why Stable Back-Office SaaS Will Win in the K-Shaped Recovery, Bidding Wars and Exits in 2027
summary:
Over the past few years, I’ve heard many conversations and read articles about the so-called “SaaSpocalypse” - and many who don’t have boots on the ground in the advisory space may believe that due to macroeconomic uncertainties, capital has evaporated from software M&A and the value of software companies will never return to what they used to be.
However, when we observe the market ourselves today, it is nothing like that. In fact, we do not see a dead SaaS investment market. Rather, we see an extreme K-shaped recovery. While average software companies experience long and drawn-out processes with little interest, the very best companies are drawing tremendous levels of interest and competitive bidding – in fact, competitive bidding is at or exceeds levels seen during the best days of the software M&A bull market.
The valuation gap between these best-in-class software companies and the rest of the market is now between $3 and $4 billion. There is a valuation gap between clear leaders in the market and those that do not. Because of these macroeconomic uncertainties, buyer psychology has changed, resulting in a strict and absolute flight to quality. High-value software businesses, based on solid financial metrics and clear structural protection from automating technology, are obtaining higher double-digit annual recurring revenue multiples. Conversely, all other software businesses are settling for reasonable two- to three-times revenue multiples or have had extreme difficulty in transacting.
This dual-track software M&A market is one we have actively navigated. In an environment where software transactions above GBP 200 million face high bars, we witness immense capital interest for top-tier assets. The sale of Origo to iPipeline (Roper Technologies) and BrightAnalytics' majority partnership with PSG Equity highlight key exit options: strategic sales versus sponsor recapitalisations. For founders, a sponsor recapitalisation offers a 'second bite at the apple' by rolling over equity into a growth partnership, though it requires a significant operational shift as founders transition from running an independent company to managing a business with a board-backed growth partner. For those in the top 25% of performers, capital is available, but the bar to reach that level remains at a historical high.
The Mechanics of the Modern Bidding War
The extreme premium currently being paid for the best-in-class software assets is indicative of the amazing imbalance between buyers’ willingness to buy and sellers’ willingness to sell. Strategic buyers with the most cash available on their balance sheets, combined with the global Private Equity industry’s historical record of having $1.2 trillion of dry powder capital waiting to be deployed, have created a flood of long-term demand for top-tier apps but with much higher levels of buyer risk aversion than ever before. No one wants to make a mistake on these types of deals in this extremely volatile environment, so everyone is increasingly drawn to the same small pool of best-in-class assets. This creates an explosive environment for the transaction process. 
We have seen instances of this dynamic already during the launch of Origo; the number of bidders who engaged in the bidding process was 2-3 times what we originally expected because of the scarcity factor at work. Buyers competing aggressively for such assets are effectively insulating them from the volatility inherent in the wider market. However, it will take time and resources to fully extract the potential value of winning these bidding wars. The most significant way to maximise your value is through rigorous examination of the technology’s underlying capabilities. 
Buyers are becoming extremely savvy when making technology acquisitions and have learned to see through the smoke-and-mirrors associated with the descriptions of AI roadmaps and a wrapper around a 3rd-party large language model. These same buyers are looking for real technical defensibility, structural moats, and high workflow gravity in any software they are seeking to acquire. The term “high workflow gravity” refers to software positioning itself at the epicentre of a customer’s daily routine/workflows. 
Therefore, any solution a customer uses with high workflow gravity has created such friction for the customer that it would be virtually impossible to remove the product from their environment. Buyers look for proprietary data routing loops, which are incredibly difficult to replicate with automated code, and for embedded middle-tier infrastructure logic within their technologies, which cannot be easily replicated or commoditised using script-based generative AI models.
The ultimate reason for Origo receiving a price premium was its role as the digital rails for the UK pensions industry. Implementing a unique piece of technology with the operational efficiency and reproducibility of Origo would take decades to replicate. In addition, the adherence to the anticipated use-case data flow has helped in the creation of long-term stickiness, as demonstrated by BrightAnalytics. Their incredible operational stickiness has been derived from the excessive complexity associated with their sophisticated data integrations and reporting. Establishing the above-mentioned technology narratives, and backing them up with objective operational metrics, is the ultimate method to preserving maximum valuation in the sale of technology businesses.
The Blueprint for a 2027 Exit
Continued improvement in the macroeconomic environment will be reflected in an increased number of exits; however, all of the current regulations and policies will remain the same as they have in the past. The previous growth-at-all-costs mentality is no longer viable. A business that achieves a balanced profile based on the Factor of 40, such as 20% growth in sales and a 20% EBITDA, will achieve a much greater premium than a business that is investing in building up its business and spending large amounts of money on chasing raw growth. Buyers now want stable, predictable businesses that can produce a reliable stream of revenue and earnings at a reasonable rate.
If your ultimate goal is to exit your business, you must create your process well in advance and not wait until your process begins to identify the weaknesses within your business.
Assess Technical Resiliency: Conduct an initial technical assessment to identify two or more concrete examples of your data mass, and conduct an independent engineering due diligence to verify them before you proceed to selling.
Establish Core Metrics: Defend your gross and net retention rates (GRR/NRR) and include higher customer switching costs in your product design.
Make the Most of Advisors: Engage corporate finance advisors six to nine months prior to an official launch date, as this affords you plenty of time to establish a rapport with target buyers, assess interest levels in the marketplace, and craft an effective financial story ahead of a formal sale.
It is still possible to achieve premium valuations in the current marketplace; however, institutional investors now require a much higher degree of institutionalisation than ever before in order to invest at this level. While capital exists for these companies, it is essential for the business owner to demonstrate sufficient evidence and support for the position that the business has moved to the right side of the K-Shaped Curve.

title: NCR Atleos Expands ATM Services Relationship With Circle K Across More Than 7,000 North American Stores
summary:
NCR Atleos Corporation, a leader in expanding self-service financial access for financial institutions, retailers and consumers, today announced a long term, multi-country ATM services relationship with Circle K, one of North America’s largest convenience and fuel retailers and a subsidiary of Alimentation Couche-Tard. Atleos was selected to manage all ATM services across more than 7,000 Circle K and Couche-Tard stores in the United States and Canada.
Atleos will drive, manage and support Circle K’s ATM program through its managed services, network capabilities and established financial institution and fintech relationships. The collaboration reinforces a shared vision to provide consumers with convenient, reliable access to cash and self-service financial services while growing in-store engagement and converting visits into retail purchases. Atleos solutions, including Allpoint, will continue to drive foot traffic by connecting consumers with participating Circle K locations for financial services and convenience retail, saving them time and money.
“Providing a seamless and consistent customer experience across our North American footprint is a key priority for Circle K,” said Kurt Fraschetti, Vice President of U.S. Merchandising for Circle K. “Atleos brings the scale, reliability and operational expertise needed to support our business today while helping us continue to meet the evolving needs of our customers. We are pleased to expand this relationship and continue delivering convenient financial access for the communities we serve.”
“Circle K serves millions of consumers across North America, and we are proud to expand our long-standing relationship with one of the world’s leading convenience retailers,” said Stuart Mackinnon, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer for Atleos. “Value and service consistency are increasingly important to consumers in their financial and retail destination choices. Pairing a relentless focus on service execution with foot traffic drivers such as Allpoint continues to power leading merchants like Circle K toward their growth objectives.”
